title: 091028-G-3421D_LONG-RANGE-RESCUE
description: SAN DIEGO - An MH-60 Jayhawk helicopter crew from Coast Guard Sector San Diego rescued five people after their sail boat capsized 197 miles southwest of San Diego, Wednesday morning.the helicopter crew found the five people in a life raft, and subsequently hoisted them into the helicopter. U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 2nd Class Jetta H. Disco

transcript.text: When we got on scene, we started searching at the last known position.
We were fortunate to have a good position because they had a modern 406E
for the give us a good position of where they had turned that on.
So immediately after passing over that position we got a call on the radio
from the people in the raft. There were five survivors in the raft
and they were calling us on their handheld radio.
They asked us to turn around and we came back towards them.
We got off of fire so we were able to easily identify their position and we had it over to where they were.
Some expert coordination by my co-pilot with talking with folks on the radio.
So we talked with them on their radio. Luckily they had a radio
and their report of the battery was dying on so we used the last few minutes of radio power
to get back to their day and they gave us their status. They were
healthy, no one was injured. The aircraft commander started the hoisting process
to lower the rest of the swimmer down and started picking up survivors.
We had a C-130 that met us down from Mayor Stations Sacramento.
They provided cover and communications relay to our guard
and from there we just returned with the passengers
and made sure they were alright. Getting to these survivors was
really a lot easier for us because they followed really good safety procedures.
They all had a lot of rotation equipment on. They all stayed together, got in the raft.
They had a flare, they had the radio, and they had everything that they needed
so that we could easily find them. So glad that they followed those procedures.
